article.title: Confederacy of Dunces
article.author: Chuck Yates
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. In 1706, over three centuries before the start of the second Trump regime, Jonathan Swift wrote, “When a true genius appears in the world, you may know him by this sign, that the dunces are all in confederacy against him.” Swift had a good eye for the absurd, and knew a dunce when he saw one, but what would he think if he could see us now, with the dunces in charge and not a single genius anywhere in sight? At least two things seem clear. First, despite what his loyal followers think, Trump has proven that he’s no genius. He may have some knack for working a room, but so does any stand-up comic worthy of the name. It doesn’t take a genius to rouse a rabble. All you have to do is keep reminding people what they’re unhappy about, what they’re afraid of, and who their enemies are. It doesn’t matter what you say. If you just keep saying it every chance you get, it isn’t long before people start believing it, and in no time you’ll be fooling all of the people all of the time. And second, though many of Trump’s most faithful supporters may be honorable men and women, there also are plenty of dunces among them. Captivated by his promise to rid the country of rats, they’ve trailed along behind him like a gaggle of enchanted children following the Pied Piper. Will they continue to follow him, though, after the chaos he’s unleashed in their lives with exorbitant tariffs, rampant inflation, vicious nationwide manhunts, and a gratuitous new war? We can’t know, but the results of the midterm election look very much like the beginning of an answer. Related: Voting for the Future of America Donald Trump, the man who would Make America Great Again, is now a lame duck, along with all of the dunces he’s placed in his cabinet and in other positions of power. With control of both houses of Congress soon to pass to the opposition, Trump’s loyal supporters there are about to become as irrelevant as his opponents were until the voters collectively roared “Enough!” and reversed the MAGA tide. The new Congress may even act to rein in the courts, ending their knee-jerk affirmation of Trump’s scofflaw policies and behavior. It looked as if the first of Trump’s dunces to go would be Pete Hegseth, who calls himself Secretary of War, but plainly understands nothing about war. Obsessed with race, gender, and muscular masculinity, Hegseth has rampaged through the senior staff of the most powerful military in the history of the planet, replacing seasoned professionals with successors qualified in his mind because they’re white, male, and motivated by a blind loyalty to their leader. Like the president who appointed him, Hegseth acts as a law unto himself, blustering along from one hair-brained idea to the next, as if he could alter reality by the sheer force of his will. Like others in Trump’s troop of dunces, he’s incapable of imagining he could be wrong. Embarrassing himself almost daily in both word and deed, he “struts and frets his hour upon the stage.” Soon enough he’ll be heard no more, and he’ll be just one more pathetic character in what has become “a tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing.” It was no surprise, then, that members of the House began impeachment proceedings against him almost as soon as the election results were in. The impeachment vote failed, but once the Republicans have become the minority, their Democratic colleagues can follow through unobstructed. Regardless of what eventually happens to Hegseth and his fellow dunces, the general election of 2028 will determine what their political fate is to be. Related: What I Learned in Nagasaki: We Are Not Innocent When We Look Away If that election continues the trend of the one just ended, Trump’s dunces no longer will be able to ignore the Constitution and the federal statutes, or to replace the rule of law with rule by law, as they try to legislate their brave new world into being. The new Congress will have the opportunity to reverse all of that, and send the dunces back to the shadows they came from after Trump rode down his golden escalator in 2015 and gave them permission to come out of hiding. With a little luck and a lot of effort, a more humane world could come into being, and something like balance could return to American politics. But the luck won’t be enough, without the effort. If we on the side of light can’t or won’t overcome our own differences and work together, not only among ourselves but also with those in the opposition who remain loyal to the ideas of 1776, we’ll just end up as a confederacy of dunces in our own right.
